Volume 32, Number 9—September 2026 Dispatch Serologic Evidence of Hantavirus Exposure in Humans, Italy, 2004–2018 Suggested citation for this article Abstract Rodentborne hantaviruses and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) circulate in northern Italy but are rarely diagnosed. We tested samples collected from 371 patients during 2004–2018 and detected LCMV IgG in 2.7% of samples and hantavirus IgG in 7.3%. Puumala virus–neutralizing antibodies were confirmed in 10 cases, indicating unrecognized local hantavirus circulation. In Europe, endemic rodentborne viruses include Old World hantaviruses (Hantaviridae) and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV; Arenaviridae) (1). Puumala virus (PUUV), carried by the bank vole (Clethrionomys glareolus), is the most widespread hantavirus in Europe. In southeastern Europe and the Balkans, Dobrava-Belgrade virus (DOBV) in yellow-necked mice (Apodemus flavicollis), and Saaremaa virus in striped field mice (A. agrarius) are also present (1). Those mouse species and other potential reservoir species, such as the Mus musculus mouse and Rattus norvegicus rat, are common in northern Italy, including the regions discussed in this article (2). DOBV and PUUV cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), and LCMV, transmitted by house mice (M. musculus), can cause febrile illness or aseptic meningitis (1). Unlike in many neighboring countries, rodentborne infections are not commonly diagnosed in Italy, although evidence of LCMV and DOBV circulation and human exposure exists (2–6). This study aimed to determine serologic evidence of hantaviruses and LCMV exposure in northwestern Italy, a region where these viruses have not been extensively studied. The study samples (n = 371, average age 59.9 years) were collected during 2004–2018 for other studies in the provinces of Novara, Biella, Vercelli, and Verbano Cusio-Ossola (Figure) and included patients with various chronic diseases, including nephrologic pathologies, alcohol abuse, hepatitis C virus infection, and liver diseases. All patients provided written informed consent, and the study was approved by the local ethics committee. In 2018, we screened patient plasma samples for PUUV, DOBV and LCMV IgG using immunofluorescence assay (IFA) as previously described (2). To further determine hantavirus antibody specificity, we tested neutralizing antibodies in 2024 and 2025 against PUUV and DOBV for samples with IgG titers >1:40 in DOBV or PUUV IgG IFA. We performed focus reduction neutralization tests (FRNTs) in Vero E6 cells according to previously published protocols (7,8). In brief, we incubated Vero E6 cells with serially diluted plasma samples and hantavirus (50 focus-forming units/well) in 24-well plates. After adsorption, we overlaid cells with MEM-agarose and incubated for 8–10 days, depending on the virus. We detected foci by immunostaining with a hantavirus-specific monoclonal antibody and horseradish peroxidase–conjugated secondary antibody, visualized with AEC (3-amino-9-ethylcarbazole) substrate. We determined neutralizing titers on the basis of the reduction in foci relative to virus-only controls; we used an 80% reduction relative to the negative control as the cutoff for enhanced specificity. Of 371 patients, 27 (7.3% [95% Wilson CI 5.0%–10.4%]) were positive for hantavirus IgG by IFA (titers 1:20–1:640) (Table 1). We further tested 11 with titers >1:40 by FRNT and detected PUUV-neutralizing activity in 10/11 of the tested samples (titers 1:80 to >1:320). Neutralization of DOBV was generally lower (titers <1:40 to 1:80). Several samples exhibited PUUV-specific neutralization with minimal or absent DOBV-neutralizing activity (Table 2). For LCMV, 10 of 371 patients (2.7% [95% Wilson CI 1.5%–4.9%]) were IgG positive (titers 1:20 to 1:40) (Table 1). Seropositive cases were geographically dispersed (Figure), and antibodies to both viruses were detected only in the region of Novara. This study detected antibodies against hantaviruses and arenaviruses in patients from a previously unstudied region of northwestern Italy. Hantavirus infections are routinely reported in neighboring countries but are rarely diagnosed in Italy; yearly cases have been reported in France, Austria, and Slovenia (9). LCMV seroprevalence (2.7%) matched previous reports from the Trentino area (2). Our hantavirus seropositivity (7.3%) was higher than the 0.2% DOBV IgG reported for forestry workers in Trentino in 2002 (2) and above the estimated 1.7% average in the general population in Italy (10). Higher seroprevalence (up to 8.8%) has been reported in occupationally rodent-exposed risk groups (5). IFA results demonstrated that plasma samples were positive for PUUV or for DOBV IgG; however, FRNT demonstrated predominantly PUUV-specific neutralizing activity, suggesting PUUV as the likely infecting virus. Neutralization against DOBV was absent or detected at low titers, consistent with serologic cross-reactivity rather than an actual DOBV infection. Only 1 sample (S52) showed reactivity to both PUUV and DOBV antigens by IFA and had a mixed neutralization profile. That finding could indicate exposure to an antigenically related hantavirus or the presence of cross-reactive antibodies. Cross-neutralizing antibody responses among hantaviruses have been documented in both acute and late-convalescent patient samples, potentially complicating serologic interpretation. Although dual exposure to both PUUV and DOBV cannot be excluded, the serologic findings do not enable a definite distinction between these possibilities (7,11) The first limitation of our study is that single-time-point sampling precluded infection timing and symptom linkage to seropositivity. Because samples were collected from chronically ill persons, the findings might not fully represent the general population, and data on risk factors, residence, and travel history were unavailable. Residence in a large metropolitan area such as Milan could argue against local transmission; however, patients’ chronic conditions and regular follow-up at the regional university hospital support predominantly local or regional exposure. Furthermore, geographic representation was uneven; most patients resided in the Novara area, potentially biasing the spatial distribution of seropositive cases. Overall, we found no clear association between serologic findings and patient group, location, or sampling timing. Most hantavirus-seropositive patients were men 36–88 years of age, consistent with reports of higher incidence of hantavirus infection in men and a predominance in the 45–64–year age group (9). The neutralization profile strongly suggested exposure to PUUV or a closely related hantavirus rather than DOBV, previously reported in Italy (2,4–6). The symptoms of PUUV and DOBV infections can vary from asymptomatic to severe and often include fever, headache, abdominal pain, backache, and nausea, occurring in the absence of respiratory symptoms (1). Although both viruses can cause HFRS, disease associated with DOBV is more severe (5%–10% fatality rate), whereas PUUV infection is typically milder (<1% fatality rate) (1), which might hinder clinical recognition. PUUV infections have been documented in neighboring countries in the Alpine region and central Europe (12–14) and, given the continuity of forest ecosystems and the distribution of the bank vole, its presence in northern Italy is plausible. Although the bank vole, the natural host of PUUV, typically inhabits forests, our study area was largely semiurban and agricultural with fragmented woodland. How human exposure occurs in such environments warrants further investigation. Of note, a recent PUUV outbreak in coastal Croatia (15) highlights the virus’s ability to emerge beyond typical bank vole habitats. Our serologic findings in a cohort of chronically ill patients in northern Italy demonstrated exposure to hantaviruses and LCMV. The rate of hantavirus antibody detection was notably high, suggesting local transmission. Together with previous reports from Italy, our findings highlight that rodentborne viruses, particularly hantaviruses, are likely endemic beyond the currently recognized regions. Because of limited data on human infections, hantaviruses remain largely underdiagnosed and neglected in Italy. Although the most recent samples in this study date from 2018, the detection of antibodies across multiple sampling years suggests sustained exposure in this region. Further studies in both rodents and humans are needed to identify endemic hantavirus species and better estimate associated risks and disease burden. Raising clinician awareness of mild forms of HFRS, such as nephropathia epidemica, and ensuring access to appropriate laboratory diagnostics are crucial for timely detection and confirmation of infections. Public health messaging would be essential to minimize exposure to rodents and their excreta, helping to prevent rodentborne diseases across Italy. Dr. Faolotto is a physician affiliated with the University Hospital in Novara, Italy, where she combines clinical practice with research. Her work has included contributions to research in infectious diseases and epidemiology, with a focus on advancing clinical knowledge and patient care. analysis.background: Rodentborne hantaviruses and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) circulate in northern Italy but are rarely diagnosed (A1, F13).
analysis.methods: Serum samples from 371 patients (2004–2018) in northwestern Italy were tested for hantavirus and LCMV IgG using immunofluorescence assay (IFA) and focus reduction neutralization tests (FRNT) (A2, F15–F24).
analysis.results: Hantavirus IgG was detected in 7.3% (95% CI 5.0–10.4%) of samples, with 10/11 cases showing Puumala virus-neutralizing antibodies (A3, F25–F28). LCMV IgG was found in 2.7% (95% CI 1.5–4.9%) (A2, F29).
analysis.contribution: This study provides first evidence of local hantavirus circulation in northwestern Italy, highlighting underdiagnosed zoonotic risks in the region (A3, F31–F35).
analysis.limitations: Lack of clinical data, cross-reactivity risks in serology, and unknown exposure sources limit interpretation (F13, F28).

analysis.summary_en: Background: Rodentborne hantaviruses and LCMV circulate in northern Italy but are underdiagnosed. Methods: 371 patients (2004–2018) were tested using IFA and FRNT. Results: 7.3% hantavirus IgG (10/11 PUUV-neutralizing) and 2.7% LCMV IgG. Contribution: Evidence of local hantavirus circulation in understudied regions. Limitations: No clinical data, cross-reactivity risks.

analysis_zh.background: 啮齿动物传播的汉坦病毒和淋巴细胞性脉络丛脑膜炎病毒(LCMV)在意大利北部存在循环,但很少被诊断(A1,F13)。
analysis_zh.methods: 采用免疫荧光法(IFA)和焦点减少中和试验(FRNT)检测了2004-2018年间意大利西北部371例患者的血清样本中汉坦病毒和LCMV的IgG抗体(A2,F15-F24)。
analysis_zh.results: 7.3%(95% CI 5.0-10.4%)的样本检测到汉坦病毒IgG,其中11例中有10例显示普马拉病毒中和抗体(A3,F25-F28)。LCMV IgG检出率为2.7%(95% CI 1.5-4.9%)(A2,F29)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 该研究首次提供了意大利西北部汉坦病毒本地循环的证据,突显了该地区未被诊断的动物源性风险(A3,F31-F35)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 缺乏临床数据、血清学检测中的交叉反应风险以及未知的暴露来源限制了结果的解释(F13,F28)。

papers.title: Watching the Ship, Missing the Forest: Why Ecological Spillover, Reservoir Ecology, and Environmental Change Remain the True Hantavirus Threats in North America.
papers.abstract: Hantavirus emergence in North America is driven by interactions among reservoir ecology, environmental variability, landscape conditions, and human exposure, with ongoing environmental change increasing spillover opportunities, altering the geography of risk, and challenging traditional public health surveillance systems.

papers.title: A 5-Adic Ultrametric Framework for Alignment-Free Phylogenetic Analysis of Hantavirus RNA Sequences
papers.abstract: We develop a non-Archimedean framework for the representation and analysis of genomic sequences based on the arithmetic and geometric structure of the ring of 5-adic integers. The proposed approach associates RNA sequences with points in a compact ultrametric space through an injective symbolic-to-arithmetic embedding that transforms genomic information into a hierarchical geometric object. We prove that the embedding is a global isometry between a natural symbolic prefix metric and the induced 5-adic metric, and we show that its image forms a compact Cantor-type subset of Z5. Building upon this representation, we formulate a continuous-time evolutionary model governed by a Vladimirov pseudo-differential operator. The resulting non-Archimedean diffusion equation provides a mathematically rigorous mechanism for describing evolutionary transitions across hierarchical genomic scales and admits an explicit fundamental solution obtained through 5-adic Fourier analysis. We further introduce a finite-resolution projection onto quotient rings of Z5 and develop an alignment-free phylogenetic inference framework based directly on the 5-adic valuation. The induced distance function is ultrametric and naturally encodes hierarchical relationships through shared symbolic prefixes. The proposed construction establishes a bridge between p-adic analysis, ultrametric geometry, pseudo-differential operators, and computational phylogenetics. As an illustration, we discuss its application to Hantavirus genomic sequences, demonstrating how hierarchical evolutionary organization can be represented within a unified non-Archimedean mathematical framework.

papers.abstract_zh: 我们开发了一种基于5-进整数环算术与几何结构的非阿基米德框架,用于基因组序列的表示与分析。该方法通过符号到算术的单射嵌入,将RNA序列关联到紧致超度量空间中的点,从而将基因组信息转化为分层几何对象。我们证明该嵌入是自然符号前缀度量与诱导的5-进度量之间的全局等距映射,并且其图像构成Z5中的紧致康托尔型子集。在此表示基础上,我们构建了一个由弗拉季米罗夫伪微分算子主导的连续时间进化模型。所得的非阿基米德扩散方程提供了描述分层基因组尺度进化转变的数学严格机制,并通过5-进傅里叶分析获得了显式基本解。我们进一步引入Z5商环上的有限分辨率投影,开发了基于5-进赋值的无需比对的系统发育推断框架。诱导的度量距离具有超度量性质,并通过共享符号前缀自然编码分层关系。该构建在p-进分析、超度量几何、伪微分算子与计算系统发育学之间建立了桥梁。作为示例,我们讨论其在汉坦病毒基因组序列中的应用,展示了如何在统一的非阿基米德数学框架中表示分层进化组织。

papers.title: Hantavirus evidence in West and Central Asia: a scoping review protocol with implications for surveillance
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are hosted mainly by rodents and other small mammals. Human infection may present as haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, nephropathia epidemica, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, or hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, although mild and non-specific febrile illness also occurs. Patterns of disease and viral circulation depend on the virus and host species, local ecology, human exposure, diagnostic practice, and the organisation of surveillance. Evidence from West and Central Asia is scattered across clinical reports, serological surveys, rodent studies, molecular investigations, and surveillance programmes for undifferentiated febrile illness. The available literature suggests that hantaviruses circulate in parts of Turkey, Iran, Kazakhstan, and the South Caucasus, but the amount and type of evidence vary markedly between countries. In several settings, detection has relied on a single serological assay, while molecular confirmation and linked human-animal surveillance remain uncommon. Other countries in the region have little or no readily identifiable published evidence. A lack of publications, however, cannot be taken to mean that viral circulation is absent. A scoping review is suited to this heterogeneous literature. The purpose is to establish what has been studied, where evidence has been generated, how infection or circulation has been assessed, and which gaps are most relevant to surveillance.

analysis.background: Hantaviruses, hosted by rodents and small mammals, require surveillance due to their potential to cause severe human disease.
analysis.main_directions: The review focuses on scattered evidence from clinical, serological, rodent, and molecular studies in West and Central Asia.
analysis.current_state: Hantavirus circulation is documented in Turkey, Iran, Kazakhstan, and the South Caucasus, but evidence quality and availability vary widely.
analysis.gaps: Limited molecular confirmation, reliance on single serological assays, and sparse data in some countries hinder understanding.
analysis.future_research: Systematic surveillance, molecular validation, and cross-country collaboration are needed to address gaps in evidence and methodology.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantaviruses hosted by rodents require surveillance due to severe human disease risks. Main directions: Scoping review of fragmented clinical, serological, and molecular evidence in West/Central Asia. Current state: Circulation confirmed in Turkey, Iran, Kazakhstan, and the South Caucasus, but evidence quality varies. Gaps: Limited molecular confirmation and sparse data in some regions. Future research: Systematic surveillance and cross-country collaboration to strengthen evidence.

papers.abstract_zh: 汉坦病毒主要由啮齿动物和其他小型哺乳动物宿主。人类感染可能表现为肾综合征出血热、流行性肾病、汉坦病毒肺综合征或汉坦病毒心肺综合征,但也可能出现轻度和非特异性发热性疾病。疾病和病毒传播的模式取决于病毒和宿主物种、当地生态、人类暴露、诊断实践和监测组织。来自西亚和中亚的证据分散在临床报告、血清学调查、啮齿动物研究、分子研究和未分化发热性疾病的监测项目中。现有文献表明,汉坦病毒在土耳其、伊朗、哈萨克斯坦和南高加索部分地区传播,但各国证据的数量和类型存在显着差异。在一些情况下,检测依赖于单一的血清学检测,而分子确认和相关的人与动物监测仍然不常见。该地区的其他国家很少或根本没有公开的易于识别的证据。然而,缺乏出版物并不意味着不存在病毒传播。范围界定审查适合这种异构文献。目的是确定研究内容、证据来源、如何评估感染或传播,以及哪些差距与监测最相关。

analysis_zh.background: 汉塞病毒由啮齿类动物和小型哺乳动物宿主,由于其可能引发严重的人类疾病,需要进行监测。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 综述聚焦于西亚和中亚地区临床、血清学、啮齿类动物和分子研究中的零散证据。
analysis_zh.current_state: 土耳其、伊朗、哈萨克斯坦和南高加索地区的汉塞病毒传播情况已有记录,但证据质量和可用性差异显著。
analysis_zh.gaps: 分子确认不足、依赖单一血清学检测方法以及部分国家数据稀少,阻碍了对病毒的全面理解。
analysis_zh.future_research: 需要系统性监测、分子验证和跨国合作,以弥补证据和方法学上的不足。

papers.title: HantaWatch: Federated Learning for Hantavirus Genomic Surveillance
papers.abstract: Abstract—Hantavirus genomic surveillance is limited by distributed sequence data, non-IID source heterogeneity, and constrained expert-review capacity. We propose HantaWatch, a federated learning framework that enables laboratories and surveillance sites to collaboratively train sequence-based models without sharing raw data. HantaWatch integrates k-mer feature extraction, source-aware federated client construction, adaptive DU-FedProx optimization, surveillance-specific model selection, and prediction-only triage. Experiments on binary and multiclass tasks show that HantaWatch supports high-risk screening, outbreak-associated prediction, clade classification, and clinical syndrome categorization while balancing predictive performance, false-negative risk, and update stability. The framework converts model output into risk scores, confidence estimates, uncertainty flags, and ranked expert-review priorities. HantaWatch therefore provides a practical, federated decision-support layer for decentralized Hantavirus surveillance, supporting expert prioritization without replacing laboratory or public health interpretation. Index Terms—Hantavirus surveillance, genomic surveillance, federated learning, adaptive federated optimization, sequence prioritization, public-health decision support.
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要—汉坦病毒基因组监测受限于分布式序列数据、非IID来源异质性以及受限的专家审阅能力。我们提出 HantaWatch,一种联邦学习框架,使实验室和监测站点能够在不共享原始数据的前提下协同训练基于序列的模型。HantaWatch 融合了 k-mer 特征提取、感知来源的联邦客户端构建、自适应 DU-FedProx 优化、监测特定的模型选择以及仅预测的分流。二分类和多分类任务的实验表明,HantaWatch 能在平衡预测性能、假阴性风险和更新稳定性的同时,支持高危筛查、疫情相关预测、分支分类和临床综合征分类。该框架将模型输出转换为风险得分、置信估计、不确定性标记以及排序的专家审阅优先级。因此,HantaWatch 为去中心化的汉坦病毒监测提供了实用的联邦决策支持层,在不取代实验室或公共卫生解释的前提下,支持专家优先级排序。索引词—汉坦病毒监测、基因组监测、联邦学习、自适应联邦优化、序列优先级、公共卫生决策支持。

papers.title: Enfermedades transmitidas por vectores: chagas, dengue, malaria y hantavirus
papers.abstract: Rol estratégico de la Atención Primaria: el personal médico de familia es fundamental para el cribado inicial, el manejo ambulatorio de los casos leves y la prevención del colapso hospitalario. Alta sospecha clínica: el diagnóstico inicial se fundamenta en vincular un síndrome febril inespecífico con un nexo epidemiológico claro (viajes recientes, picaduras o exposición a roedores/brotes cerrados). Identificación de «banderas rojas»: es prioritario reconocer los signos de alarma (como sangrado de mucosas, dolor abdominal intenso, compromiso respiratorio o descompensación cardíaca) para garantizar una derivación hospitalaria inmediata y oportuna. Acción comunitaria: la educación para el control del vector y la notificación epidemiológica son pilares indelegables en el abordaje integral desde el centro de salud.
